body.text: The Impending Demise of Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms

What separates informed decisions about Post-Quantum Cryptography in Production from costly guesswork in software? Primary context, measurable criteria, and disciplined execution form the foundation of lasting value.

Modern internet transport security relies overwhelmingly on RSA and Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) key exchanges. While secure against classical supercomputers, Shor algorithm running on a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC) will solve discrete logarithms and integer factorizations in polynomial time. To protect stored intercepted traffic against "harvest now, decrypt later" adversary campaigns, enterprise infrastructure is migrating rapidly to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
Core Mathematical and Implementation Pillars

items: Module Learning with Errors (ML-KEM / Kyber): Security rests on the hardness of finding short vectors in high-dimensional geometric integer lattices, a problem resistant to known quantum speedups.
Polynomial Ring Arithmetic over Z_q: Computations leverage Number Theoretic Transforms (NTT) over degree-256 polynomials with modulus q = 3329, enabling SIMD and AVX-512 hardware acceleration.
Constant-Time Microcode Execution: Eliminating conditional branching and cache-timing side channels to prevent secret-key leakage during polynomial rejection sampling.

Hybrid Classical-Post-Quantum Handshakes: Encapsulating session keys via both X25519 and ML-KEM-768 inside TLS 1.3 ClientHello records ensures which a zero-day flaw in new lattice mathematics cannot compromise legacy security guarantees.

body.text: Packet Overhead and MTU Fragmentation Challenges

While classical ECDH public keys measure a compact 32 bytes, Kyber-768 public keys require 1,184 bytes, and ciphertexts occupy 1,088 bytes. In TCP environments with standard 1,500-byte Maximum Transmission Units (MTUs), the combined TLS certificate chain and hybrid key exchange will cause IP fragmentation if not carefully compressed or negotiated using modern QUIC and zero-round-trip (0-RTT) transports.

body.text: The Path to Sovereign Production Hardening

Migrating global identity providers, web browsers, and banking ledgers requires rigorous compliance with FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) and FIPS 204 (ML-DSA).
